result:
The repository has nothing built. Its only code is a greeting `main()` and two smoke tests. There is also no spec yet: `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` is a research brief, and the three research files answer it. So this goes through the new-project entry. Every outcome below is a **candidate taken from the brief** (`specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md`), with facts and costs from the research files. You haven't confirmed any of them, so drop, merge or reword any that don't fit.

## Candidate outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome (what you get) | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision series for all four stages for total nonfarm (SA), over every month real vintages cover. Shows how revision scale (MAR, SD, tails) has moved over time. | Data is small, tens of MB at most: a few series with hundreds of monthly vintages each. FRED/ALFRED API limit is 120 requests/min. The number of usable vintages and how far back they go is measured by the core stage. |
| O2 | The same, by supersector, SA and NSA. | Roughly 2 × 13 series instead of 1. Same access route. Supersector vintage depth is unknown until fetched. |
| O3 | Each one- and two-month SA revision split into its NSA-sample part and its seasonal-factor part, over time. | Data is cheap, since it reuses the O1/O2 vintages. Whether the split is clean when factors are re-estimated each year is open. Only running it can tell. |
| O4 | The effect of collection days and first/second/third-closing rates on the scale of one- and two-month revisions. | Mostly your time. Collection days must be hand-built from release calendars, and closing rates come from BLS published tables. The research files differ on how far back closing rates go. Measured by its core stage. |
| O5 | A descriptive account of revision scale against real appropriations, BLS staffing and sample size, with party of the appropriators as a grouping only, and the identification limits stated. | Mostly your time: about 40 annual budget justifications, plus FedScope/OPM. All three research files agree these covariates are collinear and trending, so expect a weak answer. |
| O6 | A news-vs-noise split for each revision stage, from a latent-truth multi-vintage model. The benchmark enters as an irregular, more precise observation, with wedge-back. | Compute is unknown until one real fit is timed. Note that QCEW vintages are not archived (per the brief), which limits what the benchmark stage can see. |
| O7 | Driver effects pooled across supersectors. | Scales O6's fit time by the number of sectors. Measured once O6 runs. |
| O8 | Scale estimates that hold up across the 2003 break and 2020–22. | Modelling effort, not data. No estimate is possible before O6 runs. |
| O9 | Validation: posterior predictive checks on revision dispersion, LOO against a constant-variance baseline, pseudo-real-time checks. | Pseudo-real-time means refitting once per origin. That multiplies the O6 fit time by tens. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A: Revision data and descriptive scale (O1, O2).** Known progression: total nonfarm first, then supersectors. Every other track reads its vintages.
- **B: Seasonal vs sample (O3).** Research. It is split out because the decomposition answer stands without any driver model.
- **C: Collection interval (O4).** Research. It is split from D because the two rest on different variation. Collection interval varies sharply within the year, while capacity covariates move slowly over years. Either answer stands without the other, even though both explain revision scale.
- **D: Institutional capacity (O5).** Research, likely descriptive only.
- **E: Multi-vintage state-space model (O6–O9).** Research.
  - This split is the one to check most carefully. The brief asks for a single joint model.
  - If they are joined, B, C and D all wait on E's machinery. Split, each can first be answered with a simpler scale model on the observed revisions.
  - Feeding C and D's covariates into E would then be an item in E's ranked list.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 with uv (`.python-version`, `uv.lock`).
- From the brief, to confirm: NumPyro (NUTS), Dynamax, Blackjax only if needed, ArviZ, Polars.
- One risk to flag: whether JAX wheels exist for 3.14 is worth confirming before the first modelling stage.

**Proposed roadmap name:** `ces-revisions`, written as `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`. No file by that name exists.

**Optional probe, only if you say yes:** list the ALFRED vintages for one series, total nonfarm SA. That would firm up O1's vintage depth. It needs a FRED API key.

**One request:** please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves. Also confirm or change the five tracks, their kinds (especially the split of E from B–D), the name, and whether to run the probe.
